title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — third sense: penalty enters, not sin; two entries
pass_a_gloss: If the third, the Apostle fights you: here he distinguishes sin from sin's penalty, which he calls death. By infliction of penalty—that is, of death—death or penalty does enter, but sin does not. In his words sin's entry is one thing, death's another; the former is cause of the latter.
pass_b_english: If the third, the Apostle conflicts, who in this place distinguishes sin from the penalty of sin which he calls death. By the infliction of penalty, that is, of death, death or penalty indeed enters, but sin does not enter. One thing in the Apostle's words is the entry of sin, another the entry of death; that is the cause of this.
source_text: Si tertium, repugnat Apostolus qui peccatum hoc loco distinguit a poena peccati quam mortem vocat. Inflictione poenae, hoc est, mortis, intrat quidem mors seu poena, sed non intrat peccatum. Alius est in verbis Apostoli introitus peccati, alius introitus mortis, ille causa est huius.

choices.choice: Penalty/death enters; sin's entry is distinct cause
